channel.title: Microsoft on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Microsoft on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: commandline: Introducing Microsoft-Decision-1, our model for fast decision-making
item.description:
Microsoft introduced Microsoft-Decision-1, a decision-scoring model for structured decision tasks. It is described as optimized for low latency and high quality, and positioned as outperforming both LLMs and other decision models.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: Post-quantum authentication: Why organizations should start testing certificate ecosystems now
item.description:
Microsoft says organizations should begin testing certificate ecosystems now to prepare for post-quantum authentication. The post highlights Microsoft’s PQC TLS Pilot Program as a way to validate readiness for future post-quantum TLS deployments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: CISO perspectives on managing vulnerability risks in the age of AI
item.description:
The post says CISOs should adapt vulnerability management practices for AI-driven environments to reduce cybersecurity risk and improve resilience. It frames the topic as managing vulnerabilities in the age of AI-powered tooling and threats.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: Building an agentic system and a learning loop around customer IP
item.description:
Microsoft and Kantar built an agentic system around Kantar’s 30 years of ad metrics and frameworks to evaluate and help optimize advertisements. The system is described as part of a learning loop for customer IP.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: Insights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report
item.description:
Microsoft published a brief post pointing readers to highlights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report. The note says the security environment is becoming more interconnected, but provides no detailed findings in the excerpt.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Preparing governments for an era of interconnected cyber risk
item.description:
Microsoft says government agencies and services were the most impacted sector in 2026 cyber activity, accounting for 27% of observed activity versus 17% in 2025. The post ties this to Microsoft’s 2026 Digital Defense Report and frames it as interconnected cyber risk for governments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​Secure what’s next: Your guide to Microsoft Security at Microsoft Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s Ignite 2026 security post says the company will highlight an AI-first, end-to-end security platform. The platform is described as covering identities, devices, data, applications, clouds, infrastructure, and AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Phishing Abuses RMM Tools for Persistent Access
item.description:
Microsoft reported phishing campaigns that abused MSP360 RMM to deploy ScreenConnect and establish redundant remote-access channels for later malicious activity. The focus is on persistence and follow-on access rather than initial compromise alone.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: Retirement: Microsoft HPC Pack
item.description:
Microsoft is retiring all versions of HPC Pack. It is entering a one-year retirement period with limited retirement-only support, and end of support is August 27, 2027.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029
item.description:
Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029. Microsoft says you can keep using it until then, but recommends starting transition planning early as Azure IoT evolves.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Star Blizzard refines phishing and malware delivery with the RedFlick technique
item.description:
Microsoft says it has observed Russian state actor Star Blizzard since January 2026 using large-scale phishing, compromised website accounts, and a new malware delivery method it tracks as RedFlick. The update focuses on the actor’s improved detection evasion and delivery techniques.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Storm-3168: Agentic-driven cloud attacks using compromised service principals
item.description:
Microsoft describes Azure attacks linked to Storm-3168 using compromised service principals, including reconnaissance, resource deletion, and credential access. The post links the activity to JADEPUFFER and includes defender guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Beyond the ransomware: Tracking Storm-2570’s consistent tradecraft across deployments
item.description:
Microsoft says Storm-2570 reuses the same post-compromise tools and techniques across multiple ransomware deployments, including Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis, and BERT. The post outlines guidance for defenders to detect and disrupt the activity before ransomware is deployed.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing
item.description:
Microsoft says EvilTokens emerged as a major phishing-as-a-service platform for device code phishing, using AI-assisted lures, automated infrastructure, and token theft. In collaboration with partners, Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted its infrastructure and operations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud
item.description:
Microsoft describes an AI-assisted business email compromise campaign that impersonated executives and used fake invoices to target finance teams for ACH payment fraud. The post focuses on the attack pattern and how organizations can protect against it.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: PyRIT: Democratizing AI red teaming through open-source tooling
item.description:
PyRIT is presented as an open-source Python tool for AI red teaming that lowers the barrier for subject matter experts to test generative AI systems. The article describes its evolution toward making red teaming more accessible across many domains.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: Threat matrix: Mapping threats across cloud web applications
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the Cloud Web Applications Threat Matrix, a MITRE ATT&CK-aligned framework for understanding and prioritizing threats against cloud-hosted web applications and serverless platforms. It is intended to help defenders map attacks and identify mitigations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: Your agent’s guardrails have a bypass
item.description:
Microsoft introduced Agent Hooks, an open, framework-neutral governance contract for agent systems. It includes conformance testing and is intended to make enforcement fail closed instead of failing open when controls crash.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: When AI infrastructure becomes the target: Securing gateways and control points
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports on attacks against exposed AI infrastructure, focusing on LiteLLM gateway exploitation and related credential theft, persistence, and cryptomining activity. The post highlights gateways and other control points as targets that need protection.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Microsoft named a Leader in the Frost Radar™: Cloud Workload Protection Platforms, 2026
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a visionary leader in Frost & Sullivan’s 2026 Frost Radar for Cloud Workload Protection Platforms, citing Microsoft Defender for Cloud’s unified runtime security. The post is a brief recognition announcement with no product changes described.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: dotnet: .NET 11 Preview 7 is now available!
item.description:
Microsoft announced .NET 11 Preview 7, covering updates across libraries, runtime, SDK, C#, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, Entity Framework Core, F#, and Windows Forms. The provided excerpt does not include specific feature details.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
MAI-Code-1.1-Flash is rolling out in GitHub Copilot. It adds native vision support for image understanding and improves coding quality over MAI-Code-1-Flash.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for MDR/MXDR for the Enterprise
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for MDR/MXDR for the Enterprise. The post highlights Microsoft Defender Experts MDR as combining AI, threat intelligence, and human expertise.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​Microsoft named a Leader in the KuppingerCole Leadership Compass for Cloud Native Application Protection Platforms (CNAPP)
item.description:
Microsoft says KuppingerCole named it a Leader in the Leadership Compass for Cloud Native Application Protection Platforms (CNAPP). The provided excerpt does not include technical changes or product updates beyond that recognition.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Advance Zero Trust for AI: New tools and guidance to secure AI agents and DevSecOps
item.description:
Microsoft says it is expanding its Zero Trust for AI strategy with new tools and guidance aimed at securing AI agents and DevSecOps environments. The post highlights a broader security approach for AI and related development workflows.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: CaptiveCrunch: Midnight Blizzard targets travelers worldwide for malware delivery and credential theft
item.description:
Microsoft says Storm-2945, a sub-cluster of Midnight Blizzard, has been compromising sign-in portals at hospitality organizations since May 2026 to deliver malware to travelers and steal credentials. The campaign is named CaptiveCrunch and targets travelers worldwide.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Rethinking security for the age of AI
item.description:
Microsoft says cybersecurity is changing in the AI era and introduces a new security cyber stack called Project Perception. The post frames this as a rethink of security architecture rather than a specific product release.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Enhancing AI security through global AI red teaming
item.description:
Microsoft announced EXTRA, a global AI security initiative focused on AI safety research and red teaming. The program partners with universities, researchers, and regional experts to identify emerging AI risks and improve testing of frontier AI systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: From research to reality: An interview with Microsoft VP of Security Research Taesoo Kim
item.description:
Microsoft interviewed Taesoo Kim, VP of Security Research and head of Security FORGE Labs, about codename MDASH and the lab’s work on security research. The interview highlights a multi-model, agentic approach as a potential direction for improving security capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: Real world incident response: Microsoft and AXA XL strengthen cyber resilience
item.description:
Microsoft and AXA XL are collaborating to give cyber insurance policyholders direct access to Microsoft Incident Response services. The goal is to help organizations coordinate technical response, business decisions, and insurance actions during incidents.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Least privilege for AI agents: Identity, access, and tool binding
item.description:
Microsoft Security published a post on applying least-privilege principles to AI agents, focusing on identity, access control, tool binding, and auditing as agents become more autonomous.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Defending SaaS-based applications against ShinyHunters OAuth abuse
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported ShinyHunters-linked activity targeting SaaS-based applications through OAuth abuse, vishing, supply-chain compromise, and misconfigured guest access. The post focuses on how these techniques were used against SaaS environments and how to defend against them.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Securing our future: July 2026 progress report on Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative
item.description:
Microsoft published its July 2026 Secure Future Initiative progress report, summarizing work on secure foundations, AI-assisted defense, and broader cybersecurity readiness. The provided text is only a brief overview and does not include specific implementation details or metrics.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
